key_insight: OpenSearch-VL delivers a fully open, end-to-end recipe that makes state-of-the-art deep multimodal search agents reproducible by releasing transparent trajectory synthesis, training data, and training procedures. This enables models to perform active multimodal search, evidence verification, and multi-step reasoning with reproducible results.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of open high-quality training data, opaque trajectory synthesis pipelines, and missing training recipes that make top-tier multimodal search agents hard to reproduce.
method: Design and open-source a trajectory synthesis pipeline that generates multi-step, multimodal search demonstrations (query → retrieval → verification → reasoning).
Curate and release high-quality training datasets and annotation tools tailored for deep search behaviors across images, text, and web-like evidence.
Publish a complete training recipe and evaluation suite (model variants, hyperparameters, metrics) so practitioners can reproduce and adapt frontier multimodal search agents.
impact: Provides researchers and engineers with a transparent, reusable foundation to build, evaluate, and iterate on multimodal search agents—accelerating reproducibility, benchmarking, and real-world deployment.

paper_title: OpenSearch-VL: An Open Recipe for Frontier Multimodal Search Agents
paper_authors: Shuang Chen, Kaituo Feng, Hangting Chen, Wenxuan Huang, Dasen Dai
